audience.programmeDescription: Health Sciences, Policy & Management of Healthcare at Erasmus studies health services through economics, law, social-medical science, public policy, organisations and ethics. Its Dutch-taught, full-time BSc combines thematic study with research and practical projects.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three UCR programmes combine actual health-focused inquiry with different supporting fields. The closest emphasises population health, institutions and allocation; the second emphasises development, mental health and social conditions; the third adds prototyping, customer research and strategic planning to a health-needs foundation. These are related approaches to health and collective or organisational choices. They do not reproduce specialist Dutch health-system, insurance, health-law or quality training, or the required healthcare research placement. Business projects in the innovation option are not guaranteed to use healthcare settings. Shared rows show partial relationships; blank cells preserve other content and gaps.

concepts.label: Population health, institutions & society
concepts.concept: A population-health programme combines epidemiology, medical and health psychology, lifespan development and disease mechanisms with statistics, qualitative research and research synthesis. Economics, accounting, organisational psychology, public institutions, rights and ethics provide complementary tools for understanding collective choices and organisations. AI Ethics examines privacy, responsibility and psychological applications including clinical care. The programme sustains study of health and illness; its general legal, economic and management courses do not become Dutch health-system, health-insurance or patient-law training.

concepts.label: Lifecourse health & society
concepts.concept: This health-and-society programme centres epidemiology, health psychology, psychopathology, lifespan development, youth resilience, psychological assessment and research synthesis. Sociology, qualitative methods, public economics, organisations, rights and ethics support inquiry into health needs, social conditions and collective choices. AI Ethics adds inquiry into privacy, responsibility and psychological applications including clinical care. Introductory assessment practice and therapeutic approaches develop clinical skills academically; they do not confer professional qualification or reproduce the external degree’s integrated youth-service and healthcare-policy practice.

concepts.label: Health needs, innovation & organisations
concepts.concept: A health-needs and innovation programme combines epidemiology, patient experience, lifespan development and research synthesis with entrepreneurship, product development, customer research, marketing and digital strategy. Public economics, accounting, organisational psychology, rights and ethics support decisions about resources, users and implementation. Health courses investigate population needs and patient experience; business courses develop prototypes where feasible, customer insights and strategic plans. Their projects are not guaranteed to use healthcare settings or products. This offers related study of health needs and organisational innovation, rather than specialist health-service design, Dutch health-system training or a required healthcare placement.
